definitions.explanation: A rough idea or estimate of something, often used when one has a general sense of where something is or who is responsible.

examples.japanese: {犯人|はんにん}の{目星|めぼし}がついた。
examples.english: They have a lead on the culprit.

examples.japanese: {引|ひ}っ{越|こ}し{先|さき}の{目星|めぼし}はもうつけてある。
examples.english: I've already got my eye on a place to move to.

examples.japanese: {原因|げんいん}の{目星|めぼし}はついているが、まだ{確認|かくにん}が{必要|ひつよう}だ。
examples.english: I have a rough idea of the cause, but confirmation is still needed.

notes:
USAGE:
{目星|めぼし} is almost always used with the verb つく or つける. {目星|めぼし}がつく means to get a lead or form an estimate; {目星|めぼし}をつける means to single out a target or narrow things down.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {目星|めぼし}がつく (to get a lead, to have an idea)
- {目星|めぼし}をつける (to single out, to set one's sights on)
- {目星|めぼし}がつかない (to have no lead/clue)

SIMILAR WORDS:
{目途|めど} (also read {目処|めど}) means a prospect or target date and is more formal. {見当|けんとう} means a rough estimate or guess.
